title: Warwickshire Access to Food LLM pilot underperforms a simpler classification method
summary: Warwickshire’s LLM achieved 63% classification accuracy versus 95% for a simpler method. Faster food-access mapping remains intended; improved food access is not established.
account: Warwickshire County Council tested a locally hosted Llama 2 model to classify businesses by size and food availability, aiming to identify areas with limited access to affordable, nutritious food. The LLM achieved 63% classification accuracy, compared with 95% for a simpler approach. Processing took up to 1.5 hours per output. The council anticipated that further fine-tuning could save staff time on manual searches. The published evaluation establishes neither a time saving nor improved food access. This record retains the intended benefit alongside the unfavorable result. The source uses inconsistent model labels, so the exact configuration remains unverified.
purpose: Reduce manual search work when mapping access to affordable, nutritious food.
system: Locally hosted Llama 2 business-classification proof of concept
domain: Food access and local government analysis

ratings.reason: Staff time savings remain intended. The unfavorable accuracy and processing results do not establish an operational improvement.
Residents in areas with limited healthy-food access are intended beneficiaries. No improved food-access outcome is established.

ai_role.statement: The LLM performed the evaluated classification task. Its role is identified, but the intended beneficial contribution remains unproven.

evidence.citation: Warwickshire County Council project account published by the Local Government Association, February 3, 2025. Reports an internal proof-of-concept evaluation, not an independent outcome assessment.
